**Check.** Take $n=2$ and $f=a_0(x^2+b_1^2)(x^2+b_2^2)$ with $b_1\neq b_2$. Then $a_2=a_0(b_1^2+b_2^2)$ and $a_4=a_0b_1^2b_2^2$. Condition (2) reads $a_0a_4+a_2^2+a_4a_0\le\binom42 a_0a_4$, i.e. $a_2^2\le 4a_0a_4$. This becomes $a_0^2(b_1^2+b_2^2)^2\le 4a_0^2b_1^2b_2^2$, which simplifies to $(b_1^2-b_2^2)^2\le 0$. So (2) fails whenever $b_1^2\neq b_2^2$. The program output agrees: the member with $b=(1,2)$ gives LHS $=33$ and RHS $=24$, violating (2).

The general argument in Path 1 (Newton's inequalities plus the concavity step) also forces equal roots, so the equality case is $s_1=\cdots=s_n$.
